newsitem.title: POLAND: Conoco interested in Polish oil privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Conoco interested in Polish oil privatisation.

text.p: The U.S. company Conoco Inc., a unit of DuPont Co., is ready to invest up to $1 billion in Poland's oil sector which is slated for privatisation, an official of the firm's Polish subsidiary said on Friday.
DuPont Conoco Poland's supply and commercial marketing manager, Jaroslaw Sidorczuk, said his firm was considering buying into two large oil refineries, Refineria Gdanska SA and Petrochemia Plocka SA.

"DuPont Conoco is interested in the privatisation of the Polish oil sector, including the Gdansk and Plock refineries. The company can earmark even up to $1 billion for this purpose," Sidorczuk told a news briefing.

Under the government's privatisation scheme, the state-owned oil holding group, called Nafta Polska SA, will offer between 20 and 30 percent of shares in the country's seven refineries, possibly this year.
Investors in the refineries would gain access to the lucrative state-owned petrol distribution chain CPN SA, which owns nearly 1,400 of Poland's 4,600 stations.
The buyers would be allowed to increase their stakes in the refineries to majority holdings after investing in the modernisation of the companies.
After several years Nafta Polska, which by then will have minority stakes in the refineries and CPN, will itself be privatised, most likely through a public share issue.
DuPont Conoco Poland, set up in 1992, also plans to develop its own network of petrol stations, which operate under the Jet trade mark, Sidorczuk said.
He said the company would add 17 stations in 1997 to its existing 18 and had confirmed plans to build about 100 stations by the year 2000.
